conviction_note: Read on its own, the evidence points slightly up. Halliburton's Q3 (released 2026-10-20, after SLB last spoke) shows Middle East/Asia revenue up 8% sequentially on Saudi and Kuwait activity, which supports SLB's 'gradual Middle East recovery' Q3 base case. Against that, consensus Q4 revenue ($10.06B) already sits at management's '>$10B' Q4 guide, which assumed Middle East revenue of $2.1-2.2B (vs $1.66B in Q2) before US-Iran hostilities flared again on 3 Sept. So the print probably clears the Q3 bar and the reaction turns on whether Q4 is reaffirmed. abs_move 5.0 (event-implied 4.18%, raised because a Q4 reaffirm-or-cut and probably a first 2027 view are in play, and the last print moved +11%). p_up 53, near 50 because the decisive Q4 item is unresolved and the 25d skew (+2.1) leans mildly to downside. The findings sum to +1.0 against a scaled +0.3; the gap is the Q4 uncertainty, which sits in p_up and is not taken off the findings.

findings.finding: Halliburton's Q3 2026 release (2026-10-20, after SLB's July call) reports Middle East/Asia revenue of $1.405B, up 8% sequentially, 'primarily driven by higher activity across multiple product service lines in Saudi Arabia and Kuwait'. Its international revenue was about $3.54B, up about 3% sequentially. Its CEO said 'revenue exceeded our expectations', and the company gave a 2027 outlook of mid-single-digit growth and about 15% margins. SLB's Q3 guide (+3-4% sequential, $9.24-9.33B, against a $9.29B consensus) assumed a 'gradual Middle East recovery', with a flat Middle East costing about $150M. The largest peer's Middle East line rose 8% in the same quarter, which points to SLB landing at or above the midpoint rather than in the $150M downside case.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On 2026-07-24 a revenue beat of $8.97B vs $8.69B (about +3%), with Middle East resilience outside the war zone and data-center growth, bought +11.0%. On 2026-04-24 a Q1 hurt by the Middle East bought +2.6%. The two prints before that moved under 1%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. HAL rose 1.85% on its print day and SLB rose from 49.09 to 51.10 over 10-20/10-21, then gave all of it back on 10-22 in a sector sell-off (49.30 intraday). If the read-through were fully in the price, SLB would not be back below its pre-HAL level with puts still bid. The Q3 consensus was also cut 2.2% over 30 days, so analysts have not marked it up for the peer's Middle East number.
findings.independence: Separate from the Aramco award (a different, SLB-specific document). Arabian Drilling (Saudi Exchange filing, 2026-08-12) said its suspended offshore rigs could resume, with three restarted on 1 Aug and offshore utilisation expected to reach 100% by end of Q3: https://www.saudiexchange.sa/Resources/fsPdf/28194_3703_2026-08-12_08-33-13_en.pdf

findings.finding: On 2026-09-24 SLB announced four multi-year integrated well-construction contracts from Aramco to deliver more than 450 wells in Saudi Arabia over three years, with an optional extension of up to two years. This is direct evidence for the Saudi activity ramp that underpins the Q4 Middle East assumption and the 2027 commentary.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not a print line. SLB closed 51.43 on 2026-09-24 against 51.87 the day before, so the award itself did not move the stock.
findings.why_not_priced: Public for a month and ignored on the day. The value comes when management turns it into Q4 and 2027 numbers on the call; until then it is a headline without a revenue number.
findings.independence: Same Saudi theme as the HAL finding but a different document and an SLB-specific contract. Corroborated by https://www.energy-pedia.com/news/saudi-arabia/slb-awarded-four-multi-year-integrated-well-construction-contracts-by-aramco-205431

findings.finding: The Q4 guide (revenue >$10B, about 24% adjusted EBITDA margin, Middle East revenue of $2.1-2.2B vs $1.66B in Q2) was set on 2026-07-24. On 2026-09-03 the US and Iran 'reignited hostilities with their biggest exchange of attacks since July', and both sides declared the June interim agreement dead. Consensus Q4 revenue of $10.06B already sits at or above the guide, so a reaffirmation is in the price and any trim of the Middle East assumption or the Q4 number is the downside path.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: SLB's guidance has turned on the Middle East all year. A softer Q2 guide (RBC, 2026-04-27, 'incremental impact from Middle East disruptions') came with a +2.6% reaction because the bar had already been cut. In July, guidance for a recovery came with +11%.
findings.source_date: 2026-09-03 (event date given in the search snippet; the URL path carries no date)
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. SLB fell from 56.06 (09-11) to 48.72 (09-30), roughly 13%, and the skew is mildly positive. What is not priced is the consensus: Q4 at $10.06B / $0.80 EPS still carries the full July guide. If the market had fully priced a Q4 trim, Q4 consensus would sit below $10B.
findings.independence: Macro-to-company transmission that SLB has not confirmed, and HAL's Q3 Middle East +8% cuts against it for Q3. The Q4 guide wording comes from a secondary call summary (https://quartr.com/events/slb-n-v-slb-q2-2026_3YCy3Pqv, snippet only).

findings.finding: On 2026-08-31 SLB agreed to buy Kelvion for about $3.4B in cash plus about $0.7B of assumed debt, closing in H1 2027. In the same release it reaffirmed more than $4B of 2026 shareholder returns. H1 2026 repurchases were $1.099B, and dividends run at about $0.4B a quarter, so H2 needs roughly $2B or more of returns. The Q3 buyback figure is the first test of whether the deal slows that pace. The money buys about $2.3-2.4B of revenue (about $1.2-1.3B of it data-center) and a combined data-center target of $4.5-5B by 2028.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The data-center narrative was part of the July +11%. No print reaction on capital returns has been isolated.
findings.why_not_priced: The deal is public. Not yet visible: whether Q3 repurchases kept the H1 pace of about $550M a quarter, and how the $3.4B will be funded. A buyback slowdown would show up in the release's cash-flow table on the day.
findings.independence: Q2 release figures for the H1 buyback and the data-center trajectory: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000087347/000119312526315068/d122193dex99.htm (a different document).

findings.finding: Oilfield services sold off on the eve of the print: SLB was at 49.30 intraday on 2026-10-22 against a 51.10 close the day before (-3.5%), OIH -4.5% and HAL -3.1%. SLB enters the print 3.9% down over 20 days and 17.8% below its 52-week high, so the bar for a positive reaction is lower than it was on 10-21.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In July a pre-print discount (47.22 close) was followed by +11% on the print.
findings.why_not_priced: The entry is at the 10-22 close, so the drop is in the entry price. The finding is the sector-wide reset of expectations, not idiosyncratic SLB news. If the sell-off were SLB-specific (a leak or a pre-announcement), it would have been larger than OIH's drop, and it was smaller.

SLB's North America line ($2.24B in Q2, about 25% of revenue, mostly production systems, chemicals and drilling rather than frac) is exposed only modestly, so the net effect for SLB is small.

baseline_tension: The findings lean slightly positive (peer Middle East strength and a reset tape) against a mildly positive put skew (+2.1) and a -3.9% 20-day run-up. The skew agrees with the one real negative (Q4 guide risk), so p_up is held near 50 rather than leaning long.
lessons_applied: Lesson 3/5 (caveat reaches the number; macro-to-company not confirmed by the company): the Q4/hostilities finding shrank from -1.0 to -0.6, because HAL's own Q3 Middle East +8% argues against it for the period just reported.

Lesson 4 (financing is a question): Kelvion/buyback moved from -0.2 to +0.1. The money buys a sourced data-center revenue base ($2.3-2.4B revenue, $1.2-1.3B of it data-center) and returns were reaffirmed, so it is not a negative.
Lesson 9 (net of the rest): the HAL North America stimulation read-through shrank from -0.2 to -0.1, because SLB's North America is mostly non-frac.

Lesson 1/7 (reaction function, skew): the HAL read-through stays at +0.8, as 'a peer's print landing after the company last spoke' is the pattern that has paid. p_up was set to 53 rather than 52 after the revisions, still held near 50 by the Q4 guide risk that the skew agrees with.
